title: Text statistics analyzer
prompt:
Build a text statistics tool in Python.

Modules:
- tokenizer.py: `tokenize(text) -> list[str]`. Returns the words of the text in lower case, in order. A word is a run of letters, digits and apostrophes; apostrophes at the start or end of a word are stripped, and a run that is empty after stripping is ignored. Example: `tokenize("Hello, world! It's 2024.")` returns `["hello", "world", "it's", "2024"]`.
- stats.py:
  - `word_frequencies(tokens) -> dict[str, int]` maps each word to how many times it occurs.
  - `top_words(tokens, n) -> list[tuple[str, int]]` returns the n most frequent (word, count) pairs, sorted by count descending and then alphabetically.
  - `average_word_length(tokens) -> float` returns the mean word length, or 0.0 for an empty list.
  - `sentence_count(text) -> int` counts sentences. A sentence ends with one or more of `.`, `!` or `?` (a run like `?!` or `...` counts once). Non-empty text after the last terminator counts as one more sentence. Text with no words returns 0.
- main.py: reads ALL of standard input as one text and prints exactly these four lines:
  - `Words: <total number of tokens>`
  - `Unique: <number of distinct tokens>`
  - `Sentences: <sentence count>`
  - `Top: <w1> (<c1>), <w2> (<c2>), <w3> (<c3>)` using the 3 most frequent words (fewer if the text has fewer distinct words).

Constraints: use only the Python standard library. The entry point is main.py in the project root, guarded by `if __name__ == "__main__":`.
smoke_stdin: The cat sat. The dog ran!
